title: Apple Music Resume and Next play on iPhone Safari
acceptance: On iPhone Safari Live with Apple Music, Resume after Pause and Next both play audibly with no extra queue load after the tap, and auto-advance plays the next song with no tap. Start latency itself is RF-128.
Resume on the same song does not reload the queue (no release, prepare or setQueue); it continues the paused MusicKit item.
Track changes that need a new song keep MusicKit inside the user's tap or inside an already-playing session, chosen from an on-device probe recorded in evidence before code.
Unit tests cover resume-in-place, a seek while paused, and track change; desktop Chrome Apple Music and SoundCloud/Spotify transport do not regress.
Owner hears Start, Pause, Resume, Next, seek and auto-advance on the deployed bundle; RF-29 records it.
nextAction: Steps 1 (Resume in place) and 3 (RF-123) are on draft PR #656. Next: the owner's on-device probe on iPhone Safari with Web Inspector (pause/play, setQueue while playing, multi-song queue skip, Start timing for RF-128), then step 2 (Next, seek and auto-advance) in the same PR. Owner-gated playback PR. Coordinate with RF-108 and RF-121, which also change apple-music-adapter.ts.

evidence.summary: Investigation outcome (original scope, 'setQueue runs inside the Start gesture'): a real Start tap did play on 5G, so Start needed no change. Resume and Next failed instead, so the owner re-scoped this task to the fix and moved it to Ready in session on 2026-10-29.

Owner iPhone Safari 2026-10-28, console-driven: setQueue({songs:['1440754477']}) timed out at 20 s twice without Emulate User Gesture and resolved in 313 ms with it. runtime.ts awaits prepare (setQueue) before play().
Transport results from the owner's 2026-10-28 iPhone 5G recording; the observation is recorded once in RF-29.
Draft PR: runtime resumes a paused same-track job in place (play first, inside the tap); Apple adapter releases a timed-out queue lock.
